html:
The Battle of Moscow was fought from October 1941 to January 1942 on the approaches to Moscow, the capital of the Soviet Union. The Red Army stopped the German army and then drove it back. It was Germany's first big defeat on land in World War II.

Germany had invaded the Soviet Union in June 1941. On 2 October it began Operation Typhoon, the drive on the capital, and in two weeks surrounded over 600,000 Soviet soldiers at Vyazma and Bryansk. Then autumn rain turned the roads to mud. Stalin stayed in the city and put Georgy Zhukov in charge of its defence. When the ground froze in November the Germans pushed on, to within about 30 km of the Kremlin. They were worn out and had no winter clothing as the cold fell below minus 30 degrees. On 5 December Zhukov attacked with fresh divisions, many from Siberia. The Germans were thrown back 100 to 250 km.

Soviet losses were about a million men; German losses were far smaller but could not be replaced. Hitler took command of the army himself. The same week Japan attacked Pearl Harbor. The quick war had become a long one; see Stalingrad.
